dishes.name: Currywurst
dishes.desc: Sliced pork sausage under ketchup-curry sauce and curry powder, eaten with fries or a roll. Invented in Berlin in 1949 and sold at stands across the city.

dishes.name: Berliner Pfannkuchen
dishes.desc: Jam-filled fried doughnut dusted with sugar. Berliners call it Pfannkuchen, while the rest of Germany says Berliner.

dishes.name: Buletten
dishes.desc: Pan-fried minced-meat patties with bread roll, onion and marjoram, eaten warm with mustard or cold as a snack. The classic Berlin home-style meat dish.

dishes.name: Königsberger Klopse
dishes.desc: Veal meatballs poached in a creamy caper sauce with boiled potatoes and beetroot. Brought by East Prussian refugees and now firmly a Berlin tavern staple.

dishes.name: Eisbein with sauerkraut
dishes.desc: Boiled, cured pork knuckle served with sauerkraut and pea puree. The traditional heavy plate of Berlin taverns.

dishes.name: Döner kebab
dishes.desc: Spit-roasted meat in flatbread with salad and sauces. The Berlin-style döner, developed by Turkish immigrants here in the 1970s, is the city's everyday street meal.
